title: AI, Tech Leaders Are Lobbying Trump Health Officials in a Government-Run Chat Room
key_facts: KFF Health News reviewed thousands of Slack messages, meeting transcripts and video recordings from a Slack workspace run by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), started in August 2025 and now about 1,700 members.
Members include Microsoft, Anthropic, OpenAI, Apple, Google, Oura Health, Palantir and the venture firm 8VC; only a handful of patient advocates, doctors and hospital representatives are in it.

In February, the FDA held a listening session on conversational AI for patients with at least 35 industry organisations; it was not on the FDA public calendar and the invitation went out in the Slack chat room.

A legal expert, former FDA lawyer Joseph Daval, said the chat room resembles a federal advisory committee, which would have to meet independence and fair-balance rules; the Slack code of conduct says the group is not an advisory committee.

CMS officials told tech representatives the new Medicare App Library (about two dozen commercial apps) would be a distribution channel, and that listed apps would be prioritised for a new program that reimburses AI chatbot advice or wearable tracking.
Tech vendors argued apps should be treated as 'standing in the shoes' of a patient when they request records through the national TEFCA exchange network.

CMS declined to answer questions about the Slack workspace, including its legality; Amy Gleason, CMS chief product officer, called the Health Technology Ecosystem 'an open, voluntary technical collaboration'.
AMA chief executive John Whyte said some of these tools 'aren't ready for primetime' and that there is no liability if they get things wrong.
quote_evidence: Legal experts said the chat room resembles a federal advisory panel, which would be required to operate in public view.
CMS officials declined to answer several questions about the Slack workspace, including about its legality.
“The Health Technology Ecosystem is an open, voluntary technical collaboration.”
why_it_matters_hint: Shows how much direct access technology companies have to the officials writing the rules for AI health apps, with no public notice and a legal question unanswered.
event_date: Reporting published 9 Oct 2026; the Slack workspace began in Aug 2025 and the FDA session was in Feb 2026
notes: KFF Health News' own reporting on documents it reviewed. CMS did not answer questions on legality; one legal expert's view is not a legal finding.
